controls.name: Trial Balance closing integrity
controls.description: Total closing Debits must equal total closing Credits.
controls.note: The difference is the sum of every posting that could not be traced to a complete entry. It is disclosed, never plugged. See the Data Quality Exceptions sheet.

controls.name: Trial Balance opening integrity
controls.description: Total opening Debits must equal total opening Credits.
controls.note: Reflects unbalanced postings dated before the start of the selected period.

controls.name: General ledger completeness and footing
controls.description: Every posting in the period must appear on the ledger exactly once, and the ledger debit and credit columns must foot to the same difference as the trial balance.
controls.note: Counted from the written ledger lines against the derived postings, so a posting dropped, duplicated or rounded inconsistently between the ledger and the reported balances would show here as a non-zero difference.

controls.name: General ledger debit and credit footing
controls.description: Total Debits on the ledger less total Credits, totalled from the individual posting lines, must equal the trial balance control difference.
controls.note: The trial balance is built from per-account running balances and the ledger from individual posting lines, so this is an independent path to the same figure. Agreement is what proves the two agree; a difference means a posting was lost or double counted between them.

controls.name: Journal entries balance individually
controls.description: Every journal entry this pack derives must sum to nil. Entries that do not are listed on the Entry Balance Proof sheet.
controls.note: This is the unit an auditor actually tests. The trial balance cannot identify a broken entry, because a debit error in one transaction and a credit error in another cancel in the total. Count 277 of 2376 entries do not balance; each is listed with its own legs on the Entry Balance Proof sheet.

controls.name: Cash book continuity
controls.description: Opening + receipts - payments must equal closing for every bank.
controls.note: Proves the cash book moves continuously from the opening position to the closing position with no unexplained step. Internal transfer rows are excluded from receipts and payments because they never touch a bank account; their net movement is disclosed by C9.

controls.name: Member accounts vs trial balance
controls.description: Member credit balances less loan debit balances must equal the member-related lines in the trial balance.
controls.note: Covers savings, dues and penalties, other liabilities, member equity, other assets and loans. Excludes cash, cooperative assets, income, expenditure and retained earnings, which are not member balances. The cooperative pseudo-member is included here and reported separately in C10.

controls.name: Loan register vs loan accounts
controls.description: Sum of per-loan outstanding must equal the loan receivable balance in the trial balance.
controls.note: A difference means loan-account postings exist that do not resolve to a loan record. Those are listed individually as LOAN_DETAIL_UNATTRIBUTED and quantified in C11.

controls.name: Income detail vs trial balance
controls.description: Sum of the signed income effects must equal the trial balance income movement for the period.
controls.note: Both sides are net. A negative income header is a reversal and reduces income on both the detail sheet and the trial balance, so this control still foots.

controls.name: Expense detail vs trial balance
controls.description: Sum of the signed expenditure effects must equal the trial balance expenditure movement for the period.
controls.note: Excludes cooperative asset movements, which are an asset purchase rather than an expense. Those are reported separately in the Trial Balance and are quantified in C12.

controls.name: Internal transfer memo
controls.description: Non-cash headers are excluded from cash and income. Their net movement is disclosed as a memo only.
controls.note: Internal transfers reallocate value between member accounts; they are not income and not cash.

controls.name: Cooperative pseudo-member balance
controls.description: Movement posted against member 0000000000, which represents the cooperative itself rather than a member.
controls.note: Excluded from member net worth, consistent with the app's buildAccountBalance.

controls.name: Loan movements traceable to a loan record
controls.description: Loan account movements that cannot be matched to an individual loan record, counted and quantified.
controls.note: These movements are included in the loan receivable in the trial balance but cannot be shown against an individual loan. Unmatched count 206, net detail amount -47,038,694.

controls.name: Cooperative asset movements
controls.description: Capitalised asset movements must be reported as assets, never as expenditure.
controls.note: Confirms the Expense Detail sheet excludes capitalised asset purchases.

controls.name: One-legged non-cash entries
controls.description: Internal transfer rows that form a family of their own and so have no related row to balance them.
controls.note: These rows contribute to the trial balance control difference in C1. Count 1, net header amount 11,760. Each is listed as ONE_LEGGED_NON_CASH on the Data Quality Exceptions sheet, or summarised there when beyond the largest 200. They are overwhelmingly legacy rows that recorded a member balance without a cash leg.

controls.name: Loan receivable roll-forward
controls.description: Opening loan receivable + disbursements - principal repaid = closing loan receivable.
controls.note: Disbursements and repayments are taken from the signed loan-account details posted in the period, so the roll-forward uses the same figures the Loan Movements sheet lists. Any difference is loan-account movement that no detail row explains, and is reported rather than absorbed.

controls.name: Member credits less debits
controls.description: Total gross member credits less total gross member debits must equal the total member period movement.
controls.note: Credits and debits are counted gross, so both columns are populated and an account that was credited and debited in the same period shows both. This is the control that would fail if the columns were derived from the sign of the net movement instead.

controls.name: Liability detail vs trial balance
controls.description: Sum of signed liability effects must equal the trial balance liability movement for the period.
controls.note: Covers member liability postings (e.g. Unknown Payments) that have no enterprise detail leg. The offsetting liability account keeps the trial balance in equilibrium, so these entries do not contribute to the control difference. Confirms the Liability Detail sheet agrees with the trial balance.

controls.name: Statement of Financial Position vs trial balance
controls.description: Assets less liabilities and equity on the statement of financial position must equal the trial balance control difference.
controls.note: The statement is presented from the trial balance's own closing balances, so it must foot to the same figure. Agreement proves the statement was not built by a separate calculation that has drifted from the balances behind it. A non-zero difference on C1 appears identically here and is the source data imbalance, not a presentation error.

controls.name: Income and Expenditure vs trial balance
controls.description: The surplus on the income and expenditure statement must equal income less expenditure per the trial balance.
controls.note: The trial balance carries both income and expenditure as positive figures, so the comparison is income less expenditure. Both sides are the period movement only, which proves the statement reports the same period result the trial balance does and has not swept a prior-period balance into it.

controls.name: Cash flow statement closes onto the cash book
controls.description: Closing cash on the cash flow statement must equal total closing cash and bank balances per the cash book.
controls.note: The cash book is the authority on the movement in cash. The statement reconciles the period result to that movement, and this control proves it ends where the cash book actually ends. Items the statement cannot explain are shown on the statement as a disclosed reconciling line, not absorbed.

exceptions.title: Derived loan outstanding is negative
exceptions.explanation: Loan OGSC-ab3f329f-3762-4adb-8f53-896f71a99519 was issued for 700,000 but the postings attributed to it net to a credit of 700,000. A loan disbursement records a negative detail on the loan account; a positive one means the advance was recorded in the wrong direction, so the receivable is overstated by a credit.

It is included in the control difference quantified by C13.
